solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Daughter, being devil-possessed or divine?

indicators.note: someone possessed has a spirit dwelling within, so the daughter is held inside the other word

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
the deuce is an old euphemism for the devil, as in 'what the deuce?'

explanation.surface: A daughter who is either possessed by a demon or divine, an odd alternative for a parent to weigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possessed' makes the devil hold the daughter: DE(D)UCE. 'Divine' is not the adjective but the verb, to work something out.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to infer or work out by insight, which is what deducing a conclusion means.

clue.text: Plant with numerical identification on island

blocks.note: digital means expressed in numbers, as identification by digits is
Is is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A plant labelled with a number, growing on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is the foxglove genus, a flowering plant that is also the source of a heart drug.

clue.text: Belief is conveyed by ultimatum, not half

indicators.note: not half says only half of the word survives, the rest being dropped
conveyed by means carried inside, so the short word rides within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
an ultimatum is a final demand

explanation.surface: A conviction delivered in the form of a curtailed ultimatum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belief is' reads as the start of a sentence, but 'is' is fodder; 'not half' cuts the ultimatum word down to its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is the religious belief in a creator God who does not intervene in the world, so it is a kind of belief.

clue.text: Class engaged in tricks follows the crowd

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so the class sits inside the tricks

blocks.note: cons are swindles or tricks
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A school class taking part in pranks just goes along with everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who conforms obeys accepted norms and behaves like everyone else, which is to follow the crowd.

clue.text: Finding out about odd bits of cheap jewellery

blocks.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd
bling is flashy, often cheap jewellery

explanation.surface: Discovering something about a collection of odd pieces of costume jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: To rumble someone is British slang for seeing through them or discovering their secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumbling a scheme is informal for detecting or uncovering it, so the word means finding out about something.

clue.text: Getting down? Not getting down

blocks.note: down and under both mean below
someone standing is not getting down off their feet

explanation.surface: Two contradictory instructions, as if asking whether to get down or stay on one's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase looks like a single definition, but 'Getting' alone is it, as in 'getting the joke'; 'down?' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting in the sense of grasping or comprehending is understanding, as in 'I'm not getting it'.

clue.text: Expert away probing wine store

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so the first part goes inside the store

blocks.note: a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles
off means away, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: A specialist on leave rummaging through someone's cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is an informal British word for a scientific or technical specialist, i.e. an expert.

clue.text: Watering-hole of top people to finish with huge accusations nastily made?

blocks.note: an inn is a pub, somewhere to drink
U means upper-class, the language of top people
end and finish are synonyms
OS is short for outsize

explanation.surface: A smart bar for the elite whose evening ends in a flurry of spiteful allegations.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class and OS for outsize clothing are crossword conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: Innuendos are indirect, often snide hints or insinuations, so they are accusations made in a nasty, sly way.

clue.text: Men with weapon aloft to get dangerous animal

indicators.note: aloft means up above, and in a down clue the higher part is written first

blocks.note: a gat is slang for a gun
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers holding guns high to take on a fierce beast.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'aloft' sets the weapon above the men, so it is written first.
explanation.definitionFit: Gator is short for alligator, a large reptile that can be dangerous to humans.

clue.text: Grimaced, being given hard work around Durham region?

indicators.note: around says the hard work wraps about the region named next

blocks.note: a grind is laborious, monotonous work
County Durham is in the North East of England

explanation.surface: Someone pulled a face on being handed tough work in the area around Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a county in North East England, so its region is NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin can be a forced baring of the teeth, so grinned works loosely for grimaced, i.e. pulled a face.

clue.text: Fairly good getting brought up outside capital finally — being taken outside London, say?

indicators.note: finally picks only the very last letter of the word before it
outside says the phrase for raised wraps around the selected letter

blocks.note: decent means reasonably good
raised means brought up, as children are
the final letter of capital

explanation.surface: Something passable relocated beyond the capital, a typical move of government offices out of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' appears twice: first it wraps the letter, then in the definition it means away from the capital; 'say' shows London is just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Decentralised means moved away from a central authority or location, such as functions relocated out of a capital city.

clue.text: Brilliant, a foreign court no longer in existence

blocks.note: def is slang for excellent or brilliant
un is French for a
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A splendid court overseas that has since disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct has ceased to exist or operate, so the word describes what is no longer in existence.

clue.text: Significant empowerment, but somewhat reduced speed

indicators.note: somewhat reduced says only part of the words is kept, a run of letters lying inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A big boost in power, but one that comes with a slower pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last letter of 'Significant' and takes the first four of 'empowerment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the rate or pace at which music is played or something proceeds, a synonym for speed.

clue.text: Profession involving writer turned soldier

indicators.note: turned says the writer is flipped round to read the other way
involving means the profession takes the turned writer inside itself

blocks.note: a career is one's profession
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A career that brought in an author who later became a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer turned soldier' reads as one person's life story, but 'soldier' is the definition and 'turned' acts on the pen part alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbineer is a soldier armed with a carbine, a short rifle, so the term names a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Insult team, awful and desperate?

indicators.note: awful suggests something botched and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Abusing your own team is terrible, the act of someone at the end of their tether.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'desperate' is a loose definition: last-minute efforts are often frantic ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Last-minute measures are taken in the final moments, typically in haste and urgency, close to desperation.

clue.text: Sends up flowers after end of week?

blocks.note: Sat is short for Saturday, the end of the week
irises are flowers

explanation.surface: Someone posts flowers late in the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the flowers second; 'end of week' means a day, not the letter K.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up something is British for mocking it; satirising is ridiculing through humour, so the verbs match.

clue.text: With leader of Conservatives ousted, order change

indicators.note: ousted means thrown out, so the named letter is removed
'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Conservatives'

blocks.note: the first letter of Conservatives
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: The Tory leader has been ejected, so the party's direction is reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C out of EDICT to leave the definition's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit text is to revise or alter it, so edit is a synonym of change as a verb.

clue.text: The knight must have a win, on the other hand

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the chess notation for knight
taken as written
to gain is to win or obtain

explanation.surface: A knight insists on victory, though there is another point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: Then again is a discourse phrase introducing a contrasting thought, exactly as on the other hand does.

clue.text: Result of too much demand? Er, possibly!

blocks.note: first meaning: a lack of supply when demand outstrips it
second meaning, cryptic: ER is ERA cut short

explanation.walkthrough: The 'Er' looks like hesitation, but it is a word in its own right: era (an age) with its last letter docked, so a short age.
explanation.definitionFit: When demand exceeds supply the result is scarcity; and split in two, the word reads as a short age.

clue.text: Place of vision reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so a word is matched by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: sight, the faculty of seeing, is said the same as the answer

explanation.surface: A location reported to have been where someone saw a vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or plot of ground where something is or happens, so it is a synonym for place.

clue.text: The fellow's English, settling in European country as one granted concession

indicators.note: settling in says these letters come to rest inside the country that follows

blocks.note: France is a European country
his is the possessive of he, the fellow
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An Englishman who moves to a European country, where he is given a business concession.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchisee is the party granted a franchise, the right or concession to trade under another's brand.

clue.text: A heathen god church discarded? You could count on that

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so the church's letters leave the god's name

blocks.note: taken as written
Bacchus is the Roman god of wine
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A pagan deity whose church was abandoned, a sure thing to rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CH from BACCHUS; the definition plays on 'count on' meaning to rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for arithmetic, literally something on which you count.

clue.text: US serviceman embracing a rude Italian warlord

indicators.note: embracing means the serviceman holds the following words inside himself

blocks.note: GI is an American soldier
taken as written
ribald means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: An American soldier hugging a crude Italian commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the military leader behind the unification of Italy in the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi led irregular armies in the Italian Risorgimento, so he fits as an Italian military leader.

clue.text: What may sound like conspirator's false front?

indicators.note: sound like says the word is matched by how it is said

blocks.note: Guy Fawkes was a conspirator in the Gunpowder Plot

explanation.surface: A question about what might echo the face a plotter presents.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes plotted to blow up Parliament in 1605, so the conspirator is Guy.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or pretence that conceals the truth, i.e. a false front.

clue.text: Maiden in difficulty facing a series of steps

indicators.note: in says the maiden sits inside the word for difficulty

blocks.note: the rub is the difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman struggling as she faces a flight of stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A series of steps' looks like a staircase but means dance steps; 'facing' just puts the second part next to the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumba is a ballroom dance, i.e. a set sequence of dance steps.

clue.text: This has sea to south and east

definitions.text: This has sea to south and east

blocks.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A riddle about a place bordered by ocean on two sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the US state has the Atlantic along its southern and eastern coasts. The wordplay is just sea followed by east.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine's coastline faces the Atlantic Ocean to the south and east, so the state fits the description.

clue.text: Looks at powerless arthropods

indicators.note: powerless means without power, so the letter standing for it is removed

blocks.note: to inspect is to look at closely
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone examines helpless creepy-crawlies.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are one class of arthropods, the jointed-legged invertebrates, so this is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Cold refreshment offered by Greek woman

blocks.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman from Greece serving a chilled drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A granita is an Italian semi-frozen dessert of flavoured crushed ice, a cold treat for hot days.

clue.text: This not part of the dramatic Manhattan story?

definitions.text: This not part of the dramatic Manhattan story?

blocks.clueFragment: This not part of the dramatic Manhattan story?
blocks.note: surface reading: a bit of a play set in New York that got cut
setter's reading: the musical West Side Story, whose title names the other half of Manhattan

explanation.walkthrough: The musical is named for the western half of Manhattan, so the opposite half is pointedly not in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan divides into a western and an eastern half, and only the western one gives the famous musical its title.

clue.text: Belittle this person being entertained by head of faculty?

indicators.note: being entertained by means taken in as a guest, so this person goes inside the other part

blocks.note: a dean heads a university faculty
the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: Is the setter being put down when invited by a senior academic?
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity or standing, which is to belittle them.
